Phase 2 application - src/stage02_buffers_clock/main.c 
#include <stdio.h>
#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/clock.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"

static const uint BUFFER_INPUT_PINS[] = {PIN_CLK, PIN_BUSREQ_N, PIN_BOOT_READ_DISABLE};
static const uint BUFFER_OUTPUT_CONTACTS[] = {18, 16, 14};
static const uint BUFFER_INPUT_CONTACTS[] = {2, 4, 6};
static int held_step = -1;

static void restore_test_outputs(void) {
  z80_clock_stop();
  z80_safe_startup();
  held_step = -1;
}

static void step_buffer_output(void) {
  int next_step = held_step + 1;
  restore_test_outputs();
  if (next_step >= 6) {
    printf("DONE: safe levels restored\n");
    return;
  }
  held_step = next_step;
  unsigned index = (unsigned)held_step / 2;
  bool high = held_step % 2 != 0;
  gpio_put(BUFFER_INPUT_PINS[index], high);
  printf("GP%u -> AHCT244 input %u -> output %u: HELD %s; verification=unmeasured\n",
         BUFFER_INPUT_PINS[index], BUFFER_INPUT_CONTACTS[index],
         BUFFER_OUTPUT_CONTACTS[index], high ? "HIGH" : "LOW");
}

int main(void) {
  restore_test_outputs();
  stdio_init_all();
  printf("\nStage 2: AHCT244 clock and boot-read inhibit; CPU/SRAM absent\n");
  printf("d=held LOW/HIGH steps, 1=1kHz, 2=100kHz, 3=1MHz, x=safe restore\n");
  while (true) {
    int command = getchar_timeout_us(0);
    if (command == 'd') {
      step_buffer_output();
    } else if (command >= '1' && command <= '3') {
      restore_test_outputs();
      uint32_t hz = command == '1' ? 1000 : command == '2' ? 100000 : 1000000;
      printf(z80_clock_set_hz(hz) ? "clock_actual=%lu verification=unmeasured\n"
                                : "FAIL: clock configuration %lu\n",
             (unsigned long)z80_clock_get_hz());
    } else if (command == 'x') {
      restore_test_outputs();
    }
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}
Shared clock generation - src/common/clock.c 
#include "z80sbc/clock.h"

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"
#if defined(Z80_BANKED_PIO)
#include "z80sbc/banked_pio.h"
#include "z80sbc/gpio_mux.h"
#else
#include "hardware/clocks.h"
#include "hardware/pwm.h"
#endif

static volatile uint32_t actual_clock_hz;

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_clock_prepare_stepping)(void) {
  z80_clock_stop();
  gpio_put(PIN_CLK, 0);
  gpio_set_dir(PIN_CLK, GPIO_OUT);
  if (gpio_get_function(PIN_CLK) != GPIO_FUNC_SIO) {
    // Extend a frozen clock HIGH before the mux can create a falling edge.
    busy_wait_us_32(1);
#if defined(Z80_BANKED_PIO)
    z80_gpio_mux_select(PIN_CLK, GPIO_FUNC_SIO);
#else
    gpio_set_function(PIN_CLK, GPIO_FUNC_SIO);
#endif
  }
}

uint32_t z80_clock_get_hz(void) {
  return actual_clock_hz;
}

#if defined(Z80_BANKED_PIO)
bool z80_clock_set_hz(uint32_t hz) {
  if (!z80_banked_pio_clock_start(hz))
    return false;
  actual_clock_hz = hz;
  return true;
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_clock_stop)(void) {
  z80_banked_pio_clock_stop();
}
#else
bool z80_clock_set_hz(uint32_t hz) {
  if (hz < Z80_CLOCK_MIN_HZ || hz > Z80_CLOCK_MAX_HZ)
    return false;

  uint slice_num = pwm_gpio_to_slice_num(PIN_CLK);
  uint channel = pwm_gpio_to_channel(PIN_CLK);
  uint32_t sys_clk = clock_get_hz(clk_sys);
  uint32_t best_divider = 0;
  uint32_t best_count = 0;

  for (uint32_t divider = 1; divider <= 255; ++divider) {
    uint64_t denominator = (uint64_t)hz * divider;
    uint64_t count = ((uint64_t)sys_clk + denominator - 1u) / denominator;
    count = (count + 1u) & ~UINT64_C(1);
    if (count < 2)
      count = 2;
    if (count > 65536)
      continue;
    uint64_t product = (uint64_t)divider * count;
    uint64_t best_product = (uint64_t)best_divider * best_count;
    if (best_divider == 0 || product < best_product ||
        (product == best_product && count > best_count)) {
      best_divider = divider;
      best_count = (uint32_t)count;
    }
  }
  if (best_divider == 0)
    return false;

  z80_clock_prepare_stepping();
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  pwm_set_clkdiv_int_frac4(slice_num, (uint8_t)best_divider, 0);
  pwm_set_wrap(slice_num, (uint16_t)(best_count - 1u));
  pwm_set_chan_level(slice_num, channel, (uint16_t)(best_count / 2u));
  pwm_set_counter(slice_num, 0);
  gpio_set_function(PIN_CLK, GPIO_FUNC_PWM);
  pwm_set_enabled(slice_num, true);
  uint64_t product = (uint64_t)best_divider * best_count;
  actual_clock_hz = (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)sys_clk + product / 2u) / product);
  return true;
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_clock_stop)(void) {
  pwm_set_enabled(pwm_gpio_to_slice_num(PIN_CLK), false);
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_clock_resume)(void) {
  pwm_set_counter(pwm_gpio_to_slice_num(PIN_CLK), 0);
  gpio_set_function(PIN_CLK, GPIO_FUNC_PWM);
  pwm_set_enabled(pwm_gpio_to_slice_num(PIN_CLK), true);
}
#endif

void z80_clock_one_cycle(uint32_t half_period_us) {
  z80_clock_prepare_stepping();
  z80_clock_step_prepared(half_period_us);
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_clock_step_prepared)(uint32_t half_period_us) {
  busy_wait_us_32(half_period_us);
  gpio_put(PIN_CLK, 1);
  busy_wait_us_32(half_period_us);
  gpio_put(PIN_CLK, 0);
  // Let CPU controls, translators and input synchronizers settle before return.
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
}

void z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(unsigned int cycles,
                                 uint32_t half_period_us) {
  gpio_put(PIN_RESET_N, 0);
  for (unsigned int cycle = 0; cycle < cycles; ++cycle)
    z80_clock_one_cycle(half_period_us);
  z80_clock_stop();
}

U7 is the SN74LVC244AN eight-channel input buffer, powered from +3.3 V.

Disconnect external power and USB; keep U7 out of its socket until wiring checks pass. CPU and SRAM remain absent. Tick each channel after checking both wires at the actual socket contacts and Pico pins, and isolation from adjacent pins. Pico pin numbers below are physical pin positions, not GPIO numbers. See the Pico header reference.

Done Signal Z80 socket → U7 LVC244 input U7 LVC244 output → Pico pin BUSACK# Z80 pin 23 → U7 pin 2 U7 pin 18 → Pico pin 1 (GP0) IORQ# Z80 pin 20 → U7 pin 4 U7 pin 16 → Pico pin 2 (GP1) RD# Z80 pin 21 → U7 pin 6 U7 pin 14 → Pico pin 32 (GP27) WR# Z80 pin 22 → U7 pin 8 U7 pin 12 → Pico pin 34 (GP28) A0 Z80 pin 30 → U7 pin 11 U7 pin 9 → Pico pin 24 (GP18) A1 Z80 pin 31 → U7 pin 13 U7 pin 7 → Pico pin 25 (GP19) A2 Z80 pin 32 → U7 pin 15 U7 pin 5 → Pico pin 26 (GP20) A4 Z80 pin 34 → U7 pin 17 U7 pin 3 → Pico pin 27 (GP21) Done Check Verify existing U7 connections: pins 1/10/19 directly to common GND, pin 20 to Pico-derived +3.3 V, not +5 V, and C5, 100 nF, nearby between +3.3 V and GND Install U7: with external power and USB disconnected, confirm continuity, no adjacent-pin shorts and correct pin-1 orientation before insertion

Never connect the 5 V Z80 signals directly to the Pico; route them through U7.

The four monitored bits provide 16 distinct I/O ports. See I/O ports and services for why A4 is monitored but A3 is not, fixed terminal/disk assignments and the Phase 9/10 shared service allocation.

docs.text:
Build z80_stage03_control_inputs; UF2: build/src/stage03_mcp23s17/z80_stage03_control_inputs.uf2. Maintained application.

s samples BUSACK/IORQ/RD/WR and port. With CPU absent and pulls fitted, controls are HIGH and port is 17.

Pull each input LOW through a temporary 1 kOhm resistor; confirm only the matching GPIO/decoded bit changes and U7 outputs remain in the 3.3 V domain. Never short output pins to a rail.

Pull IORQ LOW and verify WAIT LOW. Type w to raise IO_RELEASE: WAIT must rise without either data OE becoming active.

Type x to rearm WAIT, then remove the temporary pull. This tests WAIT independently of data direction.

  • WAIT release works with data paths disabled.
  • Decoded address bits match address & 0x17, not a full 8-bit decode.

docs.title: SRAM Bank Select
docs.text:
The memory design uses one 128 KiB SRAM as two 64 KiB banks. Pico GP8 selects which half the SRAM exposes through A16. Route GP8 through U4 SN74AHCT244 level shifter so the SRAM receives a valid 5 V logic level. Do not connect Pico GPIO directly to SRAM A16.

With external power and USB disconnected, identify the contacts from the pin map. GP8 is Pico physical header pin 11; U4 pin 17 is its input and U4 pin 3 is the level-shifted output. SRAM U2 pin 2 is A16.

Done Bank-select wiring check Required connection or condition GP8 to U4 Pico physical pin 11 (GP8) connects to U4 pin 17 R24 pull-down Verify the R24 (10 kOhm) fitted in Phase 0 connects Pico physical pin 11 (GP8) to common GND. U4 to SRAM A16 U4 pin 3 connects to SRAM U2 pin 2

The pull-down holds bank 0 selected while GP8 is an input during startup. GP8 LOW selects bank 0; HIGH selects bank 1.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
With power/USB disconnected, check every actual CPU/SRAM socket contact and isolation from neighboring nets, including the GP8/U4 input net and the U4 output-to-SRAM A16 net. Confirm U4 pin 17 and SRAM U2 pin 2 have no direct connection to GND.

With power applied and CPU absent, verify pulled-up address levels.

Temporary 1 kOhm LOW tests must change only the intended monitor bit. Remove the temporary pulls afterward with power and USB disconnected. Continue to Phase 5 without inserting CPU/SRAM.

docs.title: Exception: Reset-Held Multimeter Guide for a Partially Populated Board
docs.text:
If the Z80 and SRAM are already fitted, together with Pico 2 W, U3 SN74HCT32N and U4 SN74AHCT244N, use the separate z80_reset_meter application for static measurements. U7 SN74LVC244AN, U9 SN74AHCT245N and U10 SN74LVC245AN may be absent. This is a troubleshooting exception, not permission to skip the normal population order or a Phase 4/6 pass. Do not use the ordinary Phase 2 output walk or the active address diagnostic with this partial population.

The guide never releases reset, drives the data bus, reads missing monitor buffers, or starts a free-running clock. It holds each clock HIGH and LOW on separate commands so a multimeter can settle. Six complete reset clocks are generated only as you explicitly advance through twelve held levels. The SRAM output inhibit remains asserted throughout.

docs.title: Build and open the console
docs.text:
From the repository root, using the firmware toolchain:

cmake --build build --target z80_reset_meter

UF2: build/src/stage02_buffers_clock/z80_reset_meter.uf2. The maintained application prints the full procedure, pin numbers, expected readings and next command in the USB serial console. Select the Pico USB serial port, 115200 baud (USB CDC does not use this rate for signal timing). The guide waits for the console connection before printing. Reconnecting restores safe levels and starts the guide again; a disconnected console does not leave CLK HIGH.

Before powering or flashing, verify orientations, common GND, bypasses, startup pulls, and absence of any raw 5 V connection to Pico GPIOs. All installed 5 V ICs must be powered. Apply external 5 V before USB; disconnect USB before external 5 V. Do not program this populated board with USB alone. If BOOTSEL flashing is needed, hold BOOTSEL while connecting USB after external 5 V is present. Do not change wiring or insert/remove ICs with either supply connected.

docs.title: Meter and keypress procedure
docs.text:
Use DC volts, black lead in COM and red lead in V, not the current socket. Connect black to common circuit GND. Measure named pins with the red probe, using insulated tips to avoid bridging adjacent contacts. Power off before moving clips. IC pins are numbered from the package notch/dot, not by breadboard row; U4 faces notch-down in the documented layout.

Type one command letter, then Enter. Do not paste command sequences or hold a key. An empty Enter does nothing; CR/LF/CRLF are supported.

Command Action n + Enter Acknowledge the current measurements and advance one step r + Enter Repeat current instructions without changing the held level h + Enter Show help and the current measurement instructions x Immediately stop without waiting for Enter; restore CLK LOW, RESET# LOW and read inhibit HIGH b + Enter Restart at preparation, with safe levels restored

On any unexpected voltage, press x, record the actual reading, and disconnect USB then external power before investigating. Do not advance. After x, Enter clears the discarded input line; then b + Enter restarts.

Console step Measure / expected outcome 1: preparation Confirm the hardware and meter safety instructions; CLK and RESET# held LOW 2: power U1.11, U2.32/U2.30, U3.14 and U4.20: nominal 5 V, bench target 4.75-5.25 V; Pico header 36: nominal 3.3 V, target 3.2-3.4 V; listed ground/enable/A16 pins near 0 V 3: safe outputs RESET# and CLK LOW; BUSREQ# inactive HIGH; inhibit HIGH; both data enables off; SRAM OE# HIGH. Follow every Pico/input/output endpoint printed in the console 4-15: six reset clocks Alternate one held HIGH and one held LOW per n + Enter; measure GP2/header 4 and U4.2 at approximately 3.3/0 V, and U4.18/Z80.6 at approximately 5/0 V. RESET# stays LOW and SRAM OE# stays HIGH 16: reset controls MREQ#/WR#/RD# inactive HIGH; buffered SRAM CE#/WE# and read-control outputs near 5 V 17: static HCT32 SRAM OE#, WAIT# and upward-path OE# HIGH at the listed endpoints; inhibit HIGH and IO_RELEASE LOW 18: address pulls All sixteen SRAM address pins near 5 V through the existing pulls; A16 LOW. Exact pins are printed 19: complete CLK LOW, reset asserted, no additional clocks. Save actual voltage readings; there is no automatic hardware PASS

Typical LOW target is at most 0.3 V. Pico HIGH is near 3.3 V; buffered 5 V HIGH should be within 0.5 V of its measured rail under this light load. Raw CPU HIGH is TTL and may be below 5 V (expect at least 2.4 V). These are conservative troubleshooting indications, not timing or full datasheet qualification.

The address check sees pull-ups on a floated bus, not CPU address drive. The floating 5 V data bus has no useful expected byte. This procedure cannot prove instruction execution, SRAM contents, address uniqueness, full OR-gate truth tables, clock edge quality or pulse timing. It does not replace unpowered continuity checks, the missing buffers, or Phase 6 instrument qualification.

docs.title: Optional Active Address Diagnostic
docs.text:
For all ICs installed and console control of each loader clock, use the Phase 6 console-stepped miniature loader. It writes the three specified test bytes, clears the Z80 accumulator before each read-back, and prints expected versus monitored bus behavior. It is separate from the reset-held partial-population guide above.

The same firmware now accepts f + Enter for the automatic full 64 KiB test: fill/read the sequential low-byte pattern, then fill/read the high-byte pattern, with one concise address/value/expected/SUCCESS-or-FAIL line per verified address. x aborts; all ICs and Phase 6 wiring are required.

Only after Phase 6 hardware is fitted and loader timing is qualified, build z80_stage04_address_bus; UF2 lives in build/src/stage04_address_bus/. Maintained application. a injects writes/readback at walking-one addresses; x holds reset and isolates. This is destructive RAM testing, not a held DC address generator.

Use separate analyzer captures of the complete address bus and write controls to confirm addresses actually appear during CPU writes. A successful byte readback alone cannot prove absence of all address aliases; the full-memory tests in Phase 6 are required.

docs.title: Pass Gate
docs.text:
• Sixteen distinct, correctly mapped address nets.
  • GP8 to U4 pin 17, R24 to GND, and U4 pin 3 to SRAM A16 pass unpowered continuity/isolation checks. Neither U4 pin 17 nor SRAM A16 is directly grounded.
  • No shorts.
  • Valid monitor taps.

No active-load claim is made until Phase 6.

docs.title: Maintained Source
docs.text:
The complete application below is included from the repository at documentation build time, not copied into this page. Its active diagnostic remains deferred until Phase 6.

Phase 4 application - src/stage04_address_bus/main.c 
#include <stdio.h>
#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/cpu.h"
#include "z80sbc/sram.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"
int main(void) {
  z80_safe_startup();
  stdio_init_all();
  printf("\nStage 4: CPU-driven address bus; Z80 and SRAM fitted\n");
  printf("a=walking addresses and readback, x=fail closed\n");
  while (true) {
    int command = getchar_timeout_us(0);
    if (command == 'a') {
      bool ok = z80_cpu_prepare_loader();
      for (unsigned bit = 0; ok && bit < 16; ++bit) {
        uint16_t address = (uint16_t)(1u << bit);
        uint8_t actual;
        ok = z80_sram_write_byte(address, (uint8_t)bit) &&
             z80_sram_read_byte(address, &actual) && actual == bit;
        printf("address=%04x verification=%s\n", address, ok ? "readback" : "FAIL");
        sleep_ms(250);
      }
      z80_cpu_fail_closed();
    } else if (command == 'x') z80_cpu_fail_closed();
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}

docs.title: Wiring - Bidirectional Data Path
docs.text:
U9 is the SN74AHCT245N Pico-to-5 V translator; U10 is the SN74LVC245AN 5 V-to-Pico translator. Disconnect external power and USB and keep both translators out of their sockets until wiring checks pass. CPU and SRAM remain absent.

Each row below is one shared net with branches, not a series path through a chip. Tick each row after checking every listed contact and isolation from adjacent pins. Use the connection tables below and translator reference.

docs.title: Z80 to SRAM
docs.text:
Rows are ordered by SRAM pin number, highest to lowest.

Done Signal Z80 socket → SRAM socket D7 Z80 pin 13 → SRAM pin 21 D6 Z80 pin 10 → SRAM pin 20 D5 Z80 pin 9 → SRAM pin 19 D4 Z80 pin 7 → SRAM pin 18 D3 Z80 pin 8 → SRAM pin 17 D2 Z80 pin 12 → SRAM pin 15 D1 Z80 pin 15 → SRAM pin 14 D0 Z80 pin 14 → SRAM pin 13

docs.title: Z80 to U9 AHCT245, then U10 LVC245
docs.text:
Keep the same D7-to-D0 order. Use the second free hole connected to each Z80 data pin for the hop to U9. At U9, use another hole in the same connected breadboard group for the hop to U10. The signal does not pass through U9's circuitry: all four IC contacts for a bit remain on one shared net. Tick each row after checking both hops.

Done Signal Z80 socket → U9 AHCT245 B pin U9 AHCT245 B pin → U10 LVC245 B pin D7 Z80 pin 13 → U9 pin 11 U9 pin 11 → U10 pin 11 D6 Z80 pin 10 → U9 pin 12 U9 pin 12 → U10 pin 12 D5 Z80 pin 9 → U9 pin 13 U9 pin 13 → U10 pin 13 D4 Z80 pin 7 → U9 pin 14 U9 pin 14 → U10 pin 14 D3 Z80 pin 8 → U9 pin 15 U9 pin 15 → U10 pin 15 D2 Z80 pin 12 → U9 pin 16 U9 pin 16 → U10 pin 16 D1 Z80 pin 15 → U9 pin 17 U9 pin 17 → U10 pin 17 D0 Z80 pin 14 → U9 pin 18 U9 pin 18 → U10 pin 18

docs.title: Pico-side data branches and pull-downs
docs.text:
Pico pin numbers are physical pin positions; GPIO names are in parentheses. Verify the eight individual 10 kOhm pull-downs fitted in Phase 0, not a second set. These pulls belong on the Pico side, not the 5 V data bus.

Done Signal Pico pin U9 AHCT245 A pin U10 LVC245 A pin Existing pull-down D0 Pico pin 14 (GP10) U9 pin 2 U10 pin 2 10 kOhm to GND D1 Pico pin 15 (GP11) U9 pin 3 U10 pin 3 10 kOhm to GND D2 Pico pin 16 (GP12) U9 pin 4 U10 pin 4 10 kOhm to GND D3 Pico pin 17 (GP13) U9 pin 5 U10 pin 5 10 kOhm to GND D4 Pico pin 19 (GP14) U9 pin 6 U10 pin 6 10 kOhm to GND D5 Pico pin 20 (GP15) U9 pin 7 U10 pin 7 10 kOhm to GND D6 Pico pin 21 (GP16) U9 pin 8 U10 pin 8 10 kOhm to GND D7 Pico pin 22 (GP17) U9 pin 9 U10 pin 9 10 kOhm to GND

docs.title: Supplies, directions and enables
docs.text:
Verify existing Phase 0/1/2 connections rather than adding duplicate wires or capacitors. Supply, ground and DIR links are direct wires, not resistors.

Done Pin / component Required connection U9 pin 20, VCC +5 V U9 pin 10, GND Common GND U9 pin 1, DIR +5 V: A to B U10 pin 20, VCC Pico-derived +3.3 V, not +5 V U10 pin 10, GND Common GND U10 pin 1, DIR Common GND: B to A U9 pin 19, OE# U3 HCT32 output pin 8; U3 input pin 9 receives Z80 RD# pin 21 and input pin 10 receives Pico pin 9 (GP6) U10 pin 19, OE# Pico pin 10 (GP7) C6/C7, 100 nF each C6 near U9 pin 20 across +5 V/GND; C7 near U10 pin 20 across +3.3 V/GND Installation Confirm no raw 5 V bus reaches Pico pins; verify rails, continuity, adjacent-pin isolation and pin-1 orientation before fitting U9/U10 with power and USB disconnected

Once fitted, apply external +5 V before USB and disconnect USB before removing +5 V. U9 lacks data-port power-off isolation; disabling OE does not make USB-only operation safe. Never enable both data paths at once.

docs.title: Firmware and Tests
docs.text:
Build z80_stage05_data_bus; UF2 lives in build/src/stage05_data_bus/. Maintained application.

For upward d patterns, temporarily pull raw RD# LOW through 1 kOhm with CPU absent; otherwise the HCT32 correctly keeps U9 disabled. Keep SRAM absent and boot inhibit HIGH.

Scope 00/FF/55/AA and walking-bit patterns on all eight bus lines. Verify U10 remains disabled throughout upward drive.

Remove the temporary RD pull. For i, apply weak external test pulls to D0-D7 and sample the downward path; U9 must remain disabled.

For e, reinstall the 1 kOhm raw RD# pull-down at the empty Z80 socket pin 21, keeping CPU/SRAM absent and boot inhibit HIGH. Fit external 0xAA test pulls: D1/D3/D5/D7 each through 10 kOhm to +5 V, and D0/D2/D4/D6 each through 10 kOhm to GND. Do not attach another push-pull bus driver. Disconnect USB and external power before changing any test pull, then restore external +5 V before USB.

e repeats 1000 drive/isolate/receive cycles. Capture U9 OE# pin 19 and U10 OE# pin 19: require each to go LOW in its respective phase, an interval with both HIGH between phases, and no overlapping LOW enables. Without the RD# pull-down, U9 stays disabled and the test can report PASS just by reading the external 0xAA pulls. Even with the correct fixture, byte readback alone does not prove upward drive or exclusion; retain the upward d captures and the actual-OE captures as separate pass evidence.

x isolates both paths. The software result does not measure voltage.

docs.title: Pass Gate
docs.text:
• Correct 5 V upward and 3.3 V downward levels.
  • Stable disabled paths and no simultaneous OE assertion.
  • No excessive current.
  • Remove every temporary test pull before fitting CPU/SRAM in Phase 6.

docs.title: Maintained Source
docs.text:
These complete files are included from the repository at documentation build time, not copied into this page. The shared bus module also implements the four-bit port sampling used in Phase 3.

Phase 5 application - src/stage05_data_bus/main.c 
#include <stdio.h>

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/bus.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"

static void output_data_patterns(void) {
  static const uint8_t patterns[] = {0x00, 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA};
  for (size_t index = 0; index < sizeof(patterns); ++index) {
    z80_data_bus_drive(patterns[index]);
    printf("data=%02x\n", patterns[index]);
    sleep_ms(250);
  }
  for (unsigned int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
    z80_data_bus_drive((uint8_t)(1u << bit));
    sleep_ms(100);
    z80_data_bus_drive((uint8_t)~(1u << bit));
    sleep_ms(100);
  }
  z80_data_bus_isolate();
  printf("PASS: patterns complete; verify on analyzer\n");
}

static bool data_endurance_test(void) {
  const uint8_t expected = 0xAA;
  for (unsigned int cycle = 0; cycle < 1000; ++cycle) {
    z80_data_bus_drive(expected);
    z80_data_bus_isolate();
    z80_data_bus_prepare_input();
    uint8_t actual = z80_data_bus_sample();
    z80_data_bus_isolate();
    if (actual != expected) {
      printf("FAIL: data cycle %u expected=%02x actual=%02x\n",
             cycle, expected, actual);
      return false;
    }
  }
  return true;
}

int main(void) {
  z80_safe_startup();
  stdio_init_all();
  printf("\nStage 5: data transceivers; CPU/SRAM absent\n");
    printf("d=output patterns, i=sample data, e=1000 cycles with external "
      "AA test pulls, x=isolate\n");

  while (true) {
    int command = getchar_timeout_us(0);
    if (command == 'd') {
      output_data_patterns();
    } else if (command == 'i') {
      z80_data_bus_prepare_input();
      printf("data=%02x\n", z80_data_bus_sample());
      z80_data_bus_isolate();
    } else if (command == 'e') {
      printf(data_endurance_test() ? "PASS: 1000 data interlock cycles\n"
                                   : "FAIL: data endurance\n");

    tight_loop_contents();

}

#include "z80sbc/bus.h"

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"

enum { DATA_MASK = 0xFFu << PIN_DATA_0 };
_Static_assert(PIN_DATA_7 == PIN_DATA_0 + 7, "data GPIOs must be contiguous");
_Static_assert(PIN_PORT_A1 == PIN_PORT_A0 + 1 &&
                   PIN_PORT_A2 == PIN_PORT_A0 + 2 &&
                   PIN_PORT_A4 == PIN_PORT_A0 + 3,
               "port GPIO snapshot mapping changed");

uint8_t __not_in_flash_func(z80_port_bus_sample)(void) {
  return z80_port_decode(gpio_get_all() >> PIN_PORT_A0);
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_data_bus_isolate)(void) {
  gpio_set_mask((1u << PIN_DATA_UP_OE_N) | (1u << PIN_DATA_DOWN_OE_N));
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_data_bus_drive)(uint8_t value) {
  z80_data_bus_isolate();
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  gpio_put_masked(DATA_MASK, (uint32_t)value << PIN_DATA_0);
  gpio_set_dir_masked(DATA_MASK, DATA_MASK);
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  gpio_put(PIN_DATA_UP_OE_N, 0);
}

void __not_in_flash_func(z80_data_bus_prepare_input)(void) {
  z80_data_bus_isolate();
  gpio_set_dir_masked(DATA_MASK, 0);
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  gpio_put(PIN_DATA_DOWN_OE_N, 0);
}

uint8_t __not_in_flash_func(z80_data_bus_sample)(void) {
  return (uint8_t)(gpio_get_all() >> PIN_DATA_0);
}

Clear checklist

Prerequisite: Complete the loader and RAM checks in Phase 6. Install: No additional chips; CPU was fitted in Phase 6.

This diagnostic retains the unique bus-grant and receiving-pin measurement checks formerly in the separate Phase 7. Phase 6's arithmetic and SRAM tests already provide much stronger execution coverage than this small loop, but they do not request/release the CPU bus or prove analogue reset/clock margins. There is no longer a separate Phase 7 page or firmware target; Phase 8-10 keep their existing numbers.

Do not flash this diagnostic during another running test. It is a separate, manual low-rate fixture, not a new mode in the arithmetic soak.

Build z80_stage06_bus_grant; UF2 lives in build/src/stage06_sram_dma/. Maintained application. The test image is NOP; NOP; JP 0000. It is injected, read back, then reset again before execution from SRAM.

Done Command Test l Load/verify for stepping; hold RESET afterward s Release reset on first step, clock one manual cycle with 50 ms minimum half-pulses 0/1/2/3 Reload and run at 10 Hz / 1 kHz / 100 kHz / 1 MHz r Reload/run 1 MHz q BUSREQ/BUSACK round-trip; no Pico memory drive z Reset/restart current run rate x Assert reset, disable paths, stop clock

Commands are single characters; Enter is not required. q requires a free-running mode, not manual stepping. A request or release timeout fails closed and clears the run state: start a fresh run before retrying. The diagnostic does not enable an I/O trap; its Z80 loop contains no port I/O. On a successful grant, the Pico never takes over the memory address/data bus.

Build from the repository root with the firmware toolchain:

cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DPICO_BOARD=pico2_w
cmake --build build --target z80_stage06_bus_grant

docs.title: Test Plan
docs.text:
Capture reset, first fetch at 0000, M1, CE/OE/WE and data. Both Pico data enables stay HIGH during SRAM execution and boot inhibit stays LOW.

Verify RESET# rises while CLK is stopped LOW, with at least 1 us before PWM starts. The first clock edge must meet the Z80 reset setup requirement. Verify normal fetches differ from the injected boot stream; observe the NOP/JP loop.

Measure the loaded clock at Z80 pin 6. Progress through slow rates before 1 MHz. q must float the CPU bus while BUSACK LOW without activating either Pico path; rearm I/O before releasing a grant in integrated firmware.

Test a missing BUSACK using a test-only isolated input fixture, not by shorting the CPU output. Timeout must not authorize memory access; release timeout must assert RESET and isolate. Power off before fault wiring changes.

docs.title: Maintained Source
docs.text:
These complete files are included from the repository at documentation build time, not copied into this page.

Phase 6 bus-grant diagnostic - src/stage06_sram_dma/bus_grant_test.c 
#include <stdio.h>

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/clock.h"
#include "z80sbc/cpu.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"

static const uint8_t CPU_TEST_PROGRAM[] = {
  0x00,             /* NOP */
  0x00,             /* NOP */
  0xC3, 0x00, 0x00, /* JP 0000h */
};

static bool step_image_loaded;
static uint32_t running_clock_hz;

static void stop_test(void) {
  z80_cpu_fail_closed();
  step_image_loaded = false;
  running_clock_hz = 0;
}

static bool load_and_start(uint32_t clock_hz) {
  stop_test();
  if (!z80_cpu_load_and_verify(CPU_TEST_PROGRAM, sizeof(CPU_TEST_PROGRAM)))
    return false;
  if (!z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(clock_hz))
    return false;
  running_clock_hz = clock_hz;
  return true;
}

static bool load_for_single_step(void) {
  stop_test();
  step_image_loaded = z80_cpu_load_and_verify(
      CPU_TEST_PROGRAM, sizeof(CPU_TEST_PROGRAM));
  running_clock_hz = 0;
  z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(6, 1);
  return step_image_loaded;
}

static bool single_step(void) {
  if (!step_image_loaded)
    return false;
  if (!gpio_get(PIN_RESET_N)) {
    gpio_put(PIN_BOOT_READ_DISABLE, 0);
    z80_isolate_buses();
    gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
    gpio_put(PIN_RESET_N, 1);
  }
  z80_clock_one_cycle(50000);
  return true;
}

static bool reset_running_cpu(void) {
  if (running_clock_hz == 0)
    return false;
  uint32_t clock_hz = running_clock_hz;
  stop_test();
  z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(3, 1);
  if (!z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(clock_hz))
    return false;
  running_clock_hz = clock_hz;
  return true;
}

static bool bus_round_trip(void) {
  if (running_clock_hz == 0)
    return false;
  if (!z80_cpu_request_bus(500000) || !z80_cpu_release_bus(500000)) {
    stop_test();
    return false;
  }
  return true;
}

int main(void) {
  z80_safe_startup();
  stdio_init_all();
  printf("\nStage 6: CPU reset/fetch and bus-grant qualification\n");
  printf("l=load for stepping, s=single cycle (50ms minimum half-pulses), "
      "0=run 10Hz, 1=run 1kHz, 2=run 100kHz, 3/r=run 1MHz, "
      "q=BUSREQ round-trip, z=reset/restart, x=fail closed\n");

  while (true) {
    int command = getchar_timeout_us(0);
    if (command == 'l') {
      printf(load_for_single_step() ? "PASS: image loaded; RESET# held\n"
                                    : "FAIL: image load\n");
    } else if (command == 's') {
      printf(single_step() ? "step complete\n"
                           : "FAIL: use l before stepping\n");
    } else if (command == '0') {
      printf(load_and_start(10) ? "PASS: CPU running at 10Hz\n"
                                : "FAIL: load/start\n");
    } else if (command == '1') {
      printf(load_and_start(1000) ? "PASS: CPU running at 1kHz\n"
                                  : "FAIL: load/start\n");
    } else if (command == '2') {
      printf(load_and_start(100000) ? "PASS: CPU running at 100kHz\n"
                                    : "FAIL: load/start\n");
    } else if (command == '3' || command == 'r') {
      printf(load_and_start(1000000) ? "PASS: CPU running at 1MHz\n"
                                     : "FAIL: load/start\n");
    } else if (command == 'q') {
      printf(bus_round_trip() ? "PASS: bus round-trip\n"
                              : "FAIL: start a run mode first or grant failed; inspect state\n");
    } else if (command == 'z') {
      printf(reset_running_cpu() ? "PASS: reset and restart\n"
                                 : "FAIL: start a run mode first\n");
    } else if (command == 'x') {
      stop_test();
      printf("CPU held in reset\n");
    }
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
}
Shared CPU reset and bus grants - src/common/cpu.c 
#include "z80sbc/cpu.h"

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "z80sbc/clock.h"
#include "z80sbc/pins.h"
#include "z80sbc/sram.h"
#include "z80sbc/supervisor.h"

void z80_cpu_fail_closed(void) {
  z80_isolate_buses();
  gpio_put(PIN_RESET_N, 0);
  gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
  gpio_put(PIN_BOOT_READ_DISABLE, 1);
  gpio_put(PIN_IO_RELEASE, 0);
  z80_clock_stop();
}

bool z80_cpu_prepare_loader(void) {
  z80_memory_bank_set_available(false);
  z80_cpu_fail_closed();
  z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(3, 1);
  if (!gpio_get(PIN_BUSACK_N) || !gpio_get(PIN_IORQ_N) ||
      !gpio_get(PIN_RD_N) || !gpio_get(PIN_WR_N))
    return false;
  return z80_sram_prepare_loader();
}

bool z80_cpu_load_and_verify(const uint8_t *image, uint32_t length) {
  if (image == NULL || length == 0 || length > 65536u ||
      !z80_cpu_prepare_loader())
    return false;
  bool loaded = z80_sram_load(0, image, length) &&
                z80_sram_verify(0, image, length);
  if (!loaded)
    z80_cpu_fail_closed();
  return loaded;
}

bool z80_cpu_release_reset_and_run(uint32_t clock_hz) {
  if (clock_hz < Z80_CLOCK_MIN_HZ || clock_hz > Z80_CLOCK_MAX_HZ) {
    z80_cpu_fail_closed();
    return false;
  }
  z80_isolate_buses();
  z80_reset_with_clock_cycles(6, 1);
  z80_memory_bank_select(0);
  gpio_put(PIN_BOOT_READ_DISABLE, 0);
  gpio_put(PIN_IO_RELEASE, 0);
  gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
  gpio_put(PIN_RESET_N, 1);
  busy_wait_us_32(1);
  if (!z80_clock_set_hz(clock_hz)) {
    z80_cpu_fail_closed();
    return false;
  }
  return true;
}

bool z80_cpu_request_bus(uint32_t timeout_us) {
  absolute_time_t deadline = make_timeout_time_us(timeout_us);
  z80_isolate_buses();
  gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 0);
  while (gpio_get(PIN_BUSACK_N)) {
    if (time_reached(deadline)) {
      gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
      return false;
    }
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
  return true;
}

bool z80_cpu_release_bus(uint32_t timeout_us) {
  absolute_time_t deadline = make_timeout_time_us(timeout_us);
  z80_isolate_buses();
  gpio_put(PIN_BUSREQ_N, 1);
  while (!gpio_get(PIN_BUSACK_N)) {
    if (time_reached(deadline)) {
      z80_cpu_fail_closed();
      return false;
    }
    tight_loop_contents();
  }
  return true;
}
